The Big Story · Politics & Wildlife

The ballot boxes have bells. The firecrackers are for bears.

Fukushima votes for governor today at 1,085 polling places. In part of the prefecture, election equipment now includes bear bells and firecrackers—and the voting day ends early.

Culture · Kochi · Opening today

Kochi made culture a 43-day map.

Japan’s national culture festival begins today, connecting yosakoi dance, manga, craft, food and disabled artists across one prefecture.

Kyoto · Festival · Today

Eleven floats, and wheels that still cannot turn.

Kameoka’s roughly 400-year-old autumn festival sends 11 ornate yamahoko through the former castle town from 9:30 a.m. Eight are pulled floats and three are carried; the music inherits the Gion-bayashi tradition.

Chiba · Science & Art · Today

A shogun’s residence becomes a technology lab.

Matsudo’s Science and Art Hill festival closes today at the historic Tojo-tei residence and surrounding park. The city pairs contemporary installations, talks and workshops with a 19th-century site; admission ranges from free outdoor programs to a ¥1,500 same-day ticket.

Japanese word of the day警戒 · けいかい · keikai

Vigilance; caution; being on alert. 警 means “warning” and 戒 means “to guard against.” Japanese news uses keikai for weather, crime, security and wildlife. It signals prepared attention, not panic.

Example: クマの出現に警戒する—“to stay alert for the appearance of bears.” Today it appears in maps, earlier polling hours and the extra equipment beside ballot boxes. Explore Japanese in context and learn while playing with DraMap for iOS.
